$comment: REQ-KEYS-1 (239_R7WRITE.2) — the documentation half of the reserved-chords table: per-row sources for the non-capturable set (evidence class A — facts are cited, not Playwright-provable), the keep reasons, the complete old → new table, and RV-14's layout note. Kept in a test-only module (reserved-chords-evidence.ts) so this weight never rides the entry bundle; the checker reads the slim sets from reserved-chords.json.

nonCapturableSources.mod+t: new tab — Chrome/Safari/Firefox on macOS/Windows/Linux (support.mozilla.org keyboard shortcuts; Google Chrome keyboard shortcuts; Safari keyboard shortcuts)
nonCapturableSources.mod+q: quit — Chrome/Safari on macOS (Firefox macOS also quits on ⌘Q)
nonCapturableSources.mod+tab: OS window switcher on macOS (⌘Tab) and Windows (Alt+Tab is the untrappable twin) — never delivered to the page
nonCapturableSources.ctrl+tab: next tab — Chrome/Firefox on macOS/Windows/Linux; Safari uses ⇧⌘[/] and ⌃⇧Tab equally undeliverable
nonCapturableSources.mod+shift+n: new private/incognito window — Chrome/Firefox on macOS/Windows/Linux; Safari macOS

keepReasons.mod+k: Rule 4 — the one palette chord (contextual link under a Page selection, REQ-WRITE-1); Ctrl+K is capturable so pages may claim it (RV-14e).
keepReasons.mod+enter: Rule 4 — run sheet from the Page; in Source mode CodeMirror's own Mod-Enter (insertBlankLine) wins (Rule 5).
keepReasons.mod+s: Rule 2's recorded exception — REQ-IDE save semantics: ⌘S mints a named restore point, the product's one manual save verb.

editorScopeNote: Bindings marked scope:"editor" (the ProseMirror Page keymap — marks, undo, list Tab/⇧Tab — and CodeMirror's own keys inside the Source host) are checked against Rule 1 only: inside a focused editor the USER's conventions (⌘B bold, ⌘I italic, ⌘⇧S strike, ⌘Z undo, Mod-Enter) are the expected chords, not browser-chrome collisions. The Source host's own bindings always win while it has focus (Rule 5) — the app dispatches only ⌘S there.
layoutNote: RV-14 layout note: (a) no binding in the table needs an Option/AltGr glyph on any supported layout — `alt+` chords exist only inside the findings zones (⌥J/⌥K, both printable-position-safe); (b) every `mod` chord resolves to ⌘ on macOS and Ctrl on Windows/Linux, and Ctrl+Alt on Windows overlaps AltGr — so no `mod+alt` chord is bound anywhere; (c) bare-key chords (`f`, `t`, `v`, `c`, `h`, `l`, `g`, `r`, `?`, `/`, `[`, `]`) are inert inside every text input, so a non-US layout that needs AltGr to reach `[`/`]`/`/` can still type those glyphs — the chord never fires while typing.
